sections.content: If you're searching for real estate deals in Shreveport LA, you've landed on a market that many investors are still sleeping on. Shreveport sits in the northwest corner of Louisiana, right along the Texas border, and it offers something rare in today's competitive landscape: affordable entry prices, consistent rental demand, and a growing inventory of distressed properties ripe for wholesale and fix-and-flip strategies. Whether you're a seasoned investor expanding your portfolio or just getting started, this guide will walk you through everything you need to know. If you're brand new to the game, we also recommend checking out our full guide on [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) before diving in.
Shreveport LA Market Overview: What Investors Need to Know

Shreveport is Louisiana's third-largest city with a metro population of around 400,000 people. The local economy is anchored by healthcare, education, and a growing film and entertainment sector — Louisiana's generous film tax credits have made Shreveport a legitimate production hub, earning it the nickname 'Hollywood South.' The city is also home to Barksdale Air Force Base, which provides a stable base of military tenants for landlords. These economic anchors create steady housing demand, even when broader markets fluctuate.

The Shreveport-Bossier City metro area has one of the lowest median home prices in the country. As of 2024, the median home price sits around $150,000 to $165,000, with distressed properties and fixer-uppers commonly available in the $40,000 to $90,000 range. For investors used to competing in markets like Dallas, Nashville, or Atlanta, these numbers are a breath of fresh air. The lower price point means lower capital requirements, faster returns, and more room to make mistakes and still profit — a major advantage for newer investors.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Shreveport

Not every zip code in Shreveport is created equal. Like any city, there are pockets of opportunity and areas to avoid. Here's a breakdown of the neighborhoods that are generating the most investor activity right now.
South Highlands and Highland

South Highlands is one of Shreveport's most established neighborhoods, featuring older craftsman-style homes with strong bones and great curb appeal. Properties here often need cosmetic updates but have solid ARVs in the $180,000 to $250,000 range. Highland, just adjacent, is undergoing a noticeable revitalization driven by proximity to LSUS (Louisiana State University Shreveport) and several new restaurant and retail openings. Both areas attract young professionals and are strong candidates for buy-and-hold rental strategies.
Broadmoor and Queensborough

Broadmoor is a middle-class neighborhood with a mix of owner-occupants and renters. Homes typically run between $90,000 and $160,000, and rental rates range from $900 to $1,300 per month for a three-bedroom. Queensborough offers even lower entry points — often under $80,000 for distressed properties — making it a hotspot for wholesalers and flippers targeting quick deals with strong assignment fees.
Bossier City (Just Across the River)

Bossier City is technically a separate city but functions as part of the same metro market. It has lower crime rates, newer housing stock, and strong demand from Barksdale AFB personnel. Rental properties near the base routinely achieve above-average occupancy rates, making this area a favorite for military-focused landlords. Median home prices in Bossier City are slightly higher than Shreveport proper, typically ranging from $170,000 to $220,000.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Shreveport
Wholesale Deals

Shreveport has a healthy supply of distressed and vacant properties, which means wholesalers can find motivated sellers willing to accept below-market offers. Many of these properties have delinquent taxes, probate issues, or absentee owners — all classic wholesale deal indicators. Assignment fees in Shreveport typically range from $5,000 to $20,000 per deal, depending on the ARV and condition. If you're new to this strategy, read our guide on [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) to understand the process from start to finish. You can also explore current opportunities in our [Shreveport LA market hub](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/shreveport-la).
Fix-and-Flip Opportunities

The fix-and-flip model works well in Shreveport for investors who can manage renovation costs carefully. A typical deal might look like this: purchase price of $55,000, renovation budget of $35,000, ARV of $130,000, and a sale price of $120,000 — leaving roughly $25,000 to $30,000 in gross profit before holding costs and agent fees. The key is accurate ARV estimation. Use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to run your numbers before making an offer.
Long-Term Rentals

Shreveport's rental market is strong, driven by a large renter population (approximately 48% of households rent) and consistent demand from healthcare workers, students, and military families. A three-bedroom home purchased for $100,000 can realistically generate $1,000 to $1,200 per month in rent, producing a gross rent multiplier that puts many larger markets to shame. Property taxes in Louisiana are also relatively low, which helps protect your cash flow margins.

Before running any deal in Shreveport, plug your numbers into the free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) at AIWholesail. It automatically accounts for your MAO (Maximum Allowable Offer), repair estimates, and potential profit — so you never overpay for a property.
Local Market Trends Shaping Shreveport in 2024

items: Home prices have remained relatively stable compared to national markets, with modest 2-4% annual appreciation — good for long-term holders, manageable for flippers.
Days on market for renovated retail properties averages 45-65 days, which is healthy for flippers looking to exit quickly.
New construction is limited, which keeps demand for updated existing homes consistently high.
The film and entertainment industry continues to attract young renters and short-term housing demand.
Rising insurance costs in Louisiana are a real factor — budget an extra $150 to $300 per month for landlord insurance compared to other Southern states.
Vacancy rates for well-maintained rental properties in B and C class neighborhoods hover around 5-8%, which is considered healthy for investors.
Off-market deals are abundant — probate, tax-delinquent, and absentee owner lists are fertile ground for direct mail and driving-for-dollars campaigns.

sections.content: How to Find Off-Market Deals in Shreveport

On-market MLS listings in Shreveport rarely represent the best deals — most of the real money is made off-market. Learning [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) is the single most important skill you can develop as an investor in this market. In Shreveport specifically, the most productive off-market channels include direct mail to tax-delinquent owners, probate court filings, driving for dollars in transitional neighborhoods like Queensborough and Allendale, and building relationships with local estate attorneys and property managers who know who needs to sell fast.

'The best real estate deals are never listed. They're found by investors who did the work to reach motivated sellers before anyone else knew the property was available.' — Common wisdom in the wholesale investing community
Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Shreveport

Investing remotely in Shreveport is absolutely doable, but it requires the right team on the ground. Louisiana has some unique quirks — including a legal system based on Napoleonic Code (not common law), which affects real estate contracts and title procedures. Always work with a Louisiana-licensed real estate attorney for closings, especially on wholesale deals.

items: Build your team first: Find a reliable local property manager, a licensed contractor with verified reviews, and a title company experienced in investor transactions before you make your first offer.

Understand the insurance market: Louisiana homeowner's insurance is among the most expensive in the nation due to hurricane and flood risk. Get quotes early — it directly affects your cash flow projections.
Visit before you scale: Make at least one in-person trip to drive neighborhoods, meet your team, and understand the physical reality of the market before investing remotely at scale.
Use virtual tools strategically: Platforms like AIWholesail can help you analyze deals and identify motivated sellers remotely, reducing the number of trips you need to take.

Know your exit before you enter: Shreveport's buyer pool for retail flips is solid but not enormous. Confirm your exit strategy — sell retail, rent, or wholesale to another investor — before you close on a deal.

Learn to [analyze real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) rigorously. In a market with wide price variation by neighborhood, even a few blocks can mean the difference between a great deal and a money pit.

sections.content: Request a Caddo Parish property tax report before closing on any Shreveport deal. Tax-delinquent properties can carry large back-tax liabilities that aren't always obvious from a basic title search. Your title company should catch this, but always verify independently.
Is Shreveport Right for Your Investment Strategy?

Shreveport isn't a glamour market. It won't make national headlines the way Phoenix or Austin do. But that's exactly the point. Markets like Shreveport are where disciplined investors quietly build wealth — lower competition, lower prices, and the kind of cash flow numbers that are almost impossible to find in coastal cities. If you can handle the nuances of a secondary market and build a strong local team, real estate deals in Shreveport LA can deliver consistent, meaningful returns for years to come.
